claims.statement: European Commission guidance notes that organizations can respond to procurement opportunities as a consortium, subject to operational and financial viability requirements.

contrary_evidence: Consortium participation does not remove proof-of-capacity, financial viability, or tender-specific eligibility requirements.
Many contracts may require turnover, references, bonds, or direct liability that a new coordinator cannot satisfy.

economics.acquisition_route: Family installer proof point, electrical wholesalers, trade referrals, and systematic tender monitoring
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A possible path is 30 million PLN annual managed contract value at a low-teens take rate, creating founder-owned framework and installer-network equity
economics.founder_time: Initially 15-25 hours per week; bid administration and field QA must be delegated before scale
economics.gross_margin_basis: Expected 35-55% of retained management revenue after bid costs, insurance, QA, and dispute reserves
economics.payback: Unknown; one medium framework win could repay setup, but bid loss and working-capital cycles are material
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: retain 10-18% of contract value for bid, coordination, quality, and payment administration
economics.retention_or_repeat: Multi-year frameworks and repeat member capacity can recur if delivery scores are strong

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Exclusive regional capacity, verified completion data, framework wins, and standardized QA increase bid credibility
fingerprint.customer: Retail chains, housing portfolios, enterprises, and public buyers needing multi-region energy or electrical work
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Tender feeds and framework-buyer outreach on one side; family-business, distributor, and trade referrals recruit installers on the other
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Bid preparation, capacity reservation, work allocation, common QA, evidence collection, invoicing, and SLA management
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The contracting customer pays the prime contract; the network retains a 10-18% coordination and quality margin before member payouts
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A tender's scale, geography, or service levels exceed one small installer's reach

founder_fit: Uses the parents' operating knowledge and installer credibility
Tender discovery and allocation can be heavily automated
Creates national reach without hiring every installer
Does not depend on a public personal brand
risks: The prime may bear performance, warranty, safety, and payment liability
Working-capital and bid-security needs may exceed available funds
Exclusive mandates must comply with competition and procurement law
One weak member can damage the whole network's record

structure.commercial_archetype: Managed prime contractor and tender consortium
structure.control_point: Exclusive tender-specific bidding mandates and reserved regional installation capacity
structure.critical_dependency: Member firms must meet qualification, financial, geographic, and service obligations consistently

thesis: Have vetted regional renewable and electrical installers grant tender-specific bidding and capacity-allocation mandates, then submit coordinated national bids as a prime or consortium and retain a management margin on won work.
title: Installer Joint-Tender Authority Network
uncertainties: Unknown buyer acceptance of a newly formed network
Unknown bond, insurance, turnover, and reference requirements by tender
No installer has accepted exclusivity or standardized QA
